subproblem.title: Tangent cones of a 2-dimensional minimizing cone at points p ≠ 0 are integer multiples of planes through p
subproblem.statement: For every P ∈ ℕ and every C ∈ 𝒟_2(ℝ^P) that is minimizing in ℝ^P (IsMinimizingIn C univ), has ∂C = 0 (BoundaryVanishes C) and is a cone (IsConeCurrent C), every p ∈ spt C with p ≠ 0, and every sequence λ_j > 0 with λ_j → 0: there are a strictly increasing φ : ℕ → ℕ, C' ∈ 𝒟_2(ℝ^P), an orthonormal pair τ = (τ_1, τ_2) in ℝ^P and c ∈ ℤ such that blowUp C p λ_{φ(j)} ⇀ C' in ℝ^P (ConvergesWeakly), the mass measures of these blow-ups converge to that of C' for all integer multiplicity representations (MassMeasuresConverge), p ∈ Q := span{τ_1, τ_2}, |c| ≥ 1, Θ²(μ_C, p) = |c| (HasMassDensity C p |c|), and C' = c[[Q]], i.e. C'(ω) = c∫_Q ω(x)(τ_1, τ_2) dH²(x) for every ω ∈ 𝒟²(ℝ^P), where H² = μHE[2].
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P : ℕ) (C : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) 2), IsMinimizingIn C univ → BoundaryVanishes C → IsConeCurrent C → ∀ p ∈ C.support, p ≠ 0 → ∀ (lams : ℕ → ℝ) (hlams : ∀ j, 0 < lams j), Tendsto lams atTop (𝓝 0) → ∃ (φ : ℕ → ℕ) (C' : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) 2) (τ : Fin 2 → Euclid P) (c : ℤ), StrictMono φ ∧ ConvergesWeakly (fun j => blowUp C p (lams (φ j)) (hlams (φ j)).ne') C' ∧ MassMeasuresConverge (fun j => blowUp C p (lams (φ j)) (hlams (φ j)).ne') C' ∧ Orthonormal ℝ τ ∧ p ∈ Submodule.span ℝ (Set.range τ) ∧ 1 ≤ c.natAbs ∧ HasMassDensity C p (c.natAbs : ℝ) ∧ ∀ ω : TestFormOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) 2, C' ω = (c : ℝ) * ∫ x in (Submodule.span ℝ (Set.range τ) : Set (Euclid P)), (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) 2) x τ ∂μHE[2]
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: the parent's step 4, case n − d = 2 (Simon 7.3.3(1), chapter-07.txt lines 497–510), needs the structure of 2-dimensional minimizing cones, which the book cites to [Whi82] without proof; this child supplies its first ingredient, the tangent cones of such a cone at points p ≠ 0. The argument is the book's own splitting argument for one translation direction (Lemma 3.5, lines 425–436, here in the form of the sibling result cone_splitting) followed by formula (10) of the proof of 3.3(2) (lines 547–555, the sibling result one_dim_cones) and the Constancy Theorem (Ch. 6, 2.34, the sibling child planar_constancy). Conventions. ℝ^P := Euclid P and B_ρ(x) is the open ball. For an integer multiplicity current A on an open set, μ_A denotes R.measure for any representation R of A (all representations have the same measure), M_W(A) = μ_A(W) for open W inside the domain of A, and spt A = {x in the domain : μ_A(B_ε(x)) > 0 for every ε > 0} (sibling results im_mass_measure (c), (a), (b), `Submission.dimred_im_mass_measure`); hence μ_A vanishes off spt A (Lindelöf). H² := μHE[2] and ω_2 := unitBallVolume 2. For a 2-dimensional subspace Q, H²⌞Q is the image of Lebesgue measure of ℝ² under a linear isometry (Mathlib `Isometry.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_image`, `EuclideanSpace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume`), so H²(Q ∩ B_ρ(y)) = ω_2ρ² for y ∈ Q. η_{y,λ}(w) := λ^{−1}(w − y) (Lean `dilation y λ`) and blowUp A y λ = η_{y,λ#}A. For 2-currents, M_{η_{y,λ}(W)}(η_{y,λ#}A) = λ^{−2}M_W(A) (accepted `Submission.dtc_blowUp_massOn_image`), η_{y,λ#}A has a representation with measure B ↦ λ^{−2}μ_A(η_{y,λ}^{−1}(B)) (accepted `Submission.dtc_blowUp_imrep`), and (η_{y,λ#}A)(ω) = λ^{−2}A(ω∘η_{y,λ}) (accepted `Submission.dtc_blowUp_testForm_corr`). Densities are unique: HasMassDensity A y θ and HasMassDensity A y θ' imply θ = θ' (both are ≥ 0 and ENNReal.ofReal is injective on [0, ∞)). (M) Monotonicity. Let C ∈ 𝒟_2(ℝ^P) be minimizing in ℝ^P with ∂C = 0. If P ≤ 1, every 2-covector on ℝ^P vanishes, so C = 0; hence P ≥ 2 whenever spt C ≠ ∅, and then we write P = 2 + k₀ to apply results stated in ℝ^{n+k}. ℝ^P = univ is an embedded C² P-dimensional submanifold (identity chart), closure ℝ^P ∖ ℝ^P = ∅ and spt C ⊆ ℝ^P, so the sibling result monotonicity (`Submission.dimred_minimizing_monotonicity`, with U = N = ℝ^P, n = 2, d = P) gives: ρ ↦ ρ^{−2}μ_C(B_ρ(y)) is nondecreasing on (0, ∞) for every y; Θ(y) := Θ²(μ_C, y) exists for every y (HasMassDensity C y Θ(y)) and Θ is upper semicontinuous; Θ ≥ 1 on spt C; hence μ_C(B_ρ(y)) ≥ ω_2ρ² for y ∈ spt C and ρ > 0; and Θ(y) = 0 for y ∉ spt C (a ball about y has μ_C-measure 0). (K) Cone facts. Let C ∈ 𝒟_2(ℝ^P) be a cone (IsConeCurrent C). For λ > 0 the domain of blowUp C 0 λ is η_{0,λ}(ℝ^P) = ℝ^P and currentEval(blowUp C 0 λ, ω) = C(ω), so blowUp C 0 λ = C; mass scaling gives M_{λ^{−1}W}(C) = λ^{−2}M_W(C), i.e. μ_C(sW) = s²μ_C(W) for open W and s > 0, hence for all Borel sets (outer regularity of the locally finite measure μ_C). Consequently spt C is invariant under x ↦ sx (s > 0), Θ(sx) = Θ(x), μ_C(B_ρ(0)) = ρ²μ_C(B_1(0)) for ρ > 0, and μ_C({0}) = 0.
1. (Setup.) Since p ∈ spt C, P ≥ 2 by (M); write P = 2 + k₀. ℝ^P = univ is an embedded C² (2 + k₀)-dimensional submanifold, (closure univ ∖ univ) ∩ univ = ∅, C is minimizing in univ ∩ univ and spt C ⊆ univ ∩ univ. Since ∂C = 0, boundarySupport C = spt(∂C) = spt 0 = ∅ (the zero current vanishes on every test form, so every point lies in its zero region), hence p ∈ spt C ∖ boundarySupport C.
2. (A tangent cone.) density_and_tangent_cones (2) (`Submission.density_and_tangent_cones`, with n := 2, k := ℓ := k₀, U = N = ℝ^P, T := C, x := p), applied to the sequence (λ_j), gives a strictly increasing φ and C' ∈ 𝒟_2(ℝ^P) such that C_j := blowUp C p λ_{φ(j)} ⇀ C' (ConvergesWeakly), MassMeasuresConverge (C_j) C', C' is minimizing in ℝ^P (in particular integer multiplicity) and a cone (IsConeCurrent C'), and there is θ with HasMassDensity C p θ and HasMassDensity C' 0 θ. By (M) and uniqueness of densities, θ = Θ(p) ≥ 1.
3. (∂C' = 0.) Let β ∈ 𝒟¹(ℝ^P). The domain of C_j is η_{p,λ}(ℝ^P) = ℝ^P, so currentEval(C_j, dβ) = C_j(dβ); the blow-up commutes with the boundary (accepted `Submission.dtc_blowUp_algebra` (iv)), so ∂C_j = blowUp (∂C) p λ_{φ(j)} = blowUp 0 p λ_{φ(j)} = 0 and C_j(dβ) = (∂C_j)(β) = 0. Hence C'(dβ) = lim_j currentEval(C_j, dβ) = 0, i.e. ∂C' = 0 (BoundaryVanishes C').
4. (Measures.) Let μ_j := μ_{C_j} and μ' := μ_{C'}. By the conventions, μ_j(B) = λ_{φ(j)}^{−2}μ_C(p + λ_{φ(j)}B) for Borel B, and MassMeasuresConverge gives ∫ f dμ_j → ∫ f dμ' for every continuous compactly supported f : ℝ^P → ℝ. Consequently, if s_j > 0 and s_j → 1, then s_j²∫ f(s_jy) dμ_j(y) → ∫ f dμ' for every such f: the functions f(s_j·) are supported in a fixed compact set K for large j and converge uniformly to f, and sup_j μ_j(K) < ∞ (take g ∈ C_c(ℝ^P) with g ≥ 1_K; ∫ g dμ_j converges).
5. (μ' is invariant under translations along ℝp.) Fix t ∈ ℝ. For large j put λ := λ_{φ(j)}, s := 1 + λt > 0 and λ' := λ/s. For Borel B, by (K) (μ_C(sX) = s²μ_C(X)): μ_j(B + tp) = λ^{−2}μ_C(sp + λB) = λ^{−2}s²μ_C(p + λ'B), and λ^{−2}s²μ_C(p + λ'B) = s²·λ^{−2}μ_C(p + λ(s^{−1}B)) = s²μ_j(s^{−1}B). Hence, for f ∈ C_c(ℝ^P), ∫ f(y − tp) dμ_j(y) = s_j²∫ f(s_jy) dμ_j(y) with s_j := 1 + λ_{φ(j)}t → 1. Letting j → ∞ (step 4): ∫ f(y − tp) dμ'(y) = ∫ f dμ'. As f is arbitrary, μ'(B + tp) = μ'(B) for every Borel B (uniqueness in the Riesz representation of locally finite Borel measures on ℝ^P).
6. (Invariance of the density function.) C' is a cone, so μ'(sB) = s²μ'(B) by (K). For y ∈ ℝp, λ > 0, w ∈ ℝ^P and ρ > 0, step 5 gives M_{B_ρ(y+λw)}(C') = μ'(B_ρ(λw)) = λ²μ'(B_{ρ/λ}(w)) = λ²M_{B_{ρ/λ}(w)}(C'). So the density ratio of C' at y + λw and radius ρ equals that at w and radius ρ/λ, and HasMassDensity C' w θ' implies HasMassDensity C' (y + λw) θ' for every θ'.
7. (Splitting.) The sibling result cone_splitting (`Submission.dimred_invariant_cone_splitting`) applies to S := C', n := 2 and L := span{p} (dim L = 1 < 2): C' is minimizing in ℝ^P, ∂C' = 0 (step 3), and the density hypothesis is step 6. It gives S₀ ∈ 𝒟_{2−1}(ℝ^P), minimizing in ℝ^P, with ∂S₀ = 0, a cone, spt S₀ ⊆ p^⊥, and, for t ∈ ℝp and y ∈ p^⊥: t + y ∈ spt C' ⟺ y ∈ spt S₀, and HasMassDensity C' (t + y) θ' ⟺ HasMassDensity S₀ y θ'.
8. (The one-dimensional factor.) Transport S₀ along 2 − 1 = 1 (minimality, ∂S₀ = 0, the cone property, supports and densities are preserved) and apply the sibling result one_dim_cones (`Submission.dimred_one_dim_minimizing_cone`): there are e ∈ ℝ^P and m' ∈ ℕ with (m' > 0 ⇒ |e| = 1), spt S₀ ⊆ span{e}, and HasMassDensity S₀ y m' for every y ∈ span{e}. By step 7 with t = y = 0, HasMassDensity S₀ 0 θ; also HasMassDensity S₀ 0 m'; by uniqueness, m' = θ ≥ 1, so |e| = 1. For y ∈ span{e}, the positive density m' forces y ∈ spt S₀ (if y ∉ spt S₀, a ball about y lies in the zero region of S₀, every form admissible for M_{B_ρ(y)}(S₀) with small ρ is annihilated, so M_{B_ρ(y)}(S₀) = 0 and the density would be 0). Hence span{e} ⊆ spt S₀ ⊆ p^⊥, so e ⊥ p.
9. (spt C' lies in a plane through p.) Put τ_1 := p/|p|, τ_2 := e (an orthonormal pair) and Q := span{τ_1, τ_2}, so p ∈ Q and dim Q = 2. If x ∈ spt C', write x = t + y with t := ⟨x, τ_1⟩τ_1 ∈ ℝp and y := x − t ∈ p^⊥; by step 7, y ∈ spt S₀ ⊆ span{e}, so x ∈ Q. Thus spt C' ⊆ Q.
10. (Constancy.) The sibling child planar_constancy (`Submission.idtp_planar_cycle_eq_const_mul`, with n := 2, V := ℝ^P, S := C', τ := (τ_1, τ_2)) applies: C' is integer multiplicity, ∂C' = 0, spt C' ⊆ Q, and ℝ^P ∩ Q = Q is connected. It gives c ∈ ℤ with C'(ω) = c∫_{ℝ^P∩Q} ω(x)(τ_1, τ_2) dH²(x) = c∫_Q ω(x)(τ_1, τ_2) dH²(x) for every ω ∈ 𝒟²(ℝ^P), and M_W(C') = |c|·H²(W ∩ Q) for every open W ⊆ ℝ^P. In particular M_{B_ρ(0)}(C') = |c|·ω_2ρ² for every ρ > 0, so HasMassDensity C' 0 |c|, and by uniqueness |c| = θ ≥ 1, i.e. 1 ≤ c.natAbs. By step 2, HasMassDensity C p |c|. Together with steps 2 and 9 (φ, C', τ, c) this proves the statement. ∎
proof_key_steps: P ≥ 2 and boundarySupport C = ∅; density_and_tangent_cones (2) at p gives a subsequential minimizing tangent cone C' with Θ_{C'}(0) = Θ(p) ≥ 1, and ∂C' = 0 because blow-ups of the cycle C are cycles.

Since C is a cone, a blow-up translated by tp is the blow-up at the rescaled scale λ/(1 + λt), dilated by 1 + λt; passing to the limit, μ_{C'} is invariant under translations along ℝp, so the density of C' is invariant under w ↦ y + λw (y ∈ ℝp, λ > 0).
cone_splitting with L = span{p} and one_dim_cones give a unit e ⊥ p with spt C' ⊆ Q := span{p, e} and Θ(p) = m' ∈ ℕ.
planar_constancy gives C' = c[[Q]] with |c| = Θ(p) ≥ 1.

audit.reason: The proof preserves the requested subsequence and mass convergence, proves boundary vanishing and translation invariance of the limit, and applies splitting, one-dimensional classification and planar constancy. It obtains p ∈ Q, the signed current formula and the positive integral density required by the exact type.
